title: Electromagnetic Spectrum
learning_goal: Compare applications of different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

stages.title: 1. One family of waves
stages.content: All electromagnetic waves are transverse waves that travel through a vacuum at the same speed, approximately 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, but they differ in frequency, wavelength, and photon energy.

stages.title: 2. Spectrum order
stages.content: From lowest frequency to highest: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma ray.

stages.title: 3. Frequency and wavelength
stages.content: Because c = fλ in a vacuum, higher frequency means shorter wavelength.

stages.title: 4. Applications
stages.content: Radio waves are used in communication, microwaves in communication and heating, infrared in thermal imaging, visible light in vision, ultraviolet in sterilization, X-rays in imaging, and gamma rays in some medical treatments.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Which has the higher frequency: infrared radiation or ultraviolet radiation?
stages.hint: Recall the spectrum order around visible light.
stages.alternate_explanation: Infrared lies below visible light in frequency, while ultraviolet lies above visible light.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, order spectrum regions, compare frequency and wavelength, connect each region to common applications, and explain that all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum.
